bugs: DispatchCrmSync counts and claims a subscriber even when ShouldBeUnique drops the dispatch, so it prints 'Queued 1' when nothing was pushed. My probe hit this when a job had been waiting in the queue for more than 15 minutes (app/Console/Commands/DispatchCrmSync.php:25-29). Cosmetic: no duplicate is created.
antipatterns: Two de-duplication systems: a DB claim with a 15-minute TTL plus a 3600s UniqueFor lock. They have different lifetimes, and the gap between them causes the misleading count (app/Jobs/SyncSubscriberToCrm.php:18, app/Models/Subscriber.php:15)
Uses an old-style `scopeNeedsCrmSync` method. Laravel 12+ prefers the #[Scope] attribute (app/Models/Subscriber.php:17)
Unused `$subscribers` and `$attempt` variables, and a redundant 'queue.failed.driver' config override in tests (tests/Feature/CrmSyncTest.php:57,58,120)
The test named 'lets a failed CRM call throw so the queue retries and records it in failed_jobs' only checks that handle() throws (tests/Feature/CrmSyncTest.php:44)
strengths: Finds all four root causes: the swallowed exception, re-dispatching rows that are already queued, the 24h default mutex from withoutOverlapping(), and chunk() paging over a column it is changing (fixed with chunkById)

Claims rows with an atomic conditional UPDATE, reusing a model scope in both the select and the claim. Stale claims (15 minutes) let failed subscribers reach the CRM later without flooding failed_jobs
Modern queue attributes (#[Tries], #[Backoff], #[Timeout], #[UniqueFor], #[DeleteWhenMissingModels]). The probe showed a deleted subscriber no longer produces a failed_jobs row
Adds an idempotency guard (fresh()->crm_synced_at) and a failed() hook that records the error
Tests run a real database queue: retries ending in failed_jobs, and no stacked duplicate jobs. A stale-claim test checks which subscriber was re-queued

bugs: DispatchCrmSync was not changed. It still selects every unsynced row each minute, bumps crm_sync_queued_at and reports it as queued, while ShouldBeUnique quietly drops the dispatch. The probe printed 'Queued 1 subscribers.' with no job pushed (app/Console/Commands/DispatchCrmSync.php:21-24)

During an outage there is no cooldown. failed() clears crm_sync_queued_at, and the next minute's dispatch re-queues the subscriber straight away (probe: a new job right after failure). A long outage therefore writes a new failed_jobs row per subscriber every few minutes and keeps hammering the CRM (app/Jobs/SyncSubscriberToCrm.php:57-62)

Duplicates come back when the backlog outlives UniqueFor(3600): the probe found 2 jobs for one subscriber after 70 minutes. This is the 'queue backed up' symptom the task describes (app/Jobs/SyncSubscriberToCrm.php:18)
antipatterns: Catches, updates crm_last_error, then rethrows, which duplicates what failed() already does (app/Jobs/SyncSubscriberToCrm.php:48-52)
WithoutOverlapping keeps releaseAfter=0, so an overlapping job is released immediately in a hot loop. Tries(10) was raised to absorb this instead of fixing it (app/Jobs/SyncSubscriberToCrm.php:33)
Clearing crm_sync_queued_at in failed() has no effect, because the dispatch query never filters on that column (app/Jobs/SyncSubscriberToCrm.php:60)
The mutex test asserts expiresAt <= 60, which is a loose bound for a value of 10 (tests/Feature/CrmSyncTest.php:107)
strengths: Smallest diff. The withoutOverlapping(10) and chunkById fixes are correct
Adds expireAfter(60) to the job's WithoutOverlapping so a killed worker cannot leave a permanent lock
Adds an idempotency guard against re-syncing
Best end-to-end test: a real database worker through an outage, then failed_jobs, then recovery and re-queue

bugs: A subscriber that fails permanently waits the full 60-minute CLAIM_MINUTES before being retried (probe: no re-queue at 20 minutes, re-queued at 70). Acceptable, but slow recovery after a short outage. Not a correctness bug.
antipatterns: Uses old-style public $tries/$timeout properties and a backoff() method where Laravel 12+ queue attributes would fit (app/Jobs/SyncSubscriberToCrm.php:16-25)
The test 'retries with backoff and enough attempts to survive overlap releases' only checks config, and it contradicts the dontRelease() middleware (tests/Feature/CrmSyncReliabilityTest.php:38)
Uses Http::swap(new Factory) to reset fakes where Http::fakeSequence would be cleaner (tests/Feature/CrmSyncReliabilityTest.php:51)
The stale-claim condition is inline, not in a reusable scope, so the claim duplicates part of the outer query (app/Console/Commands/DispatchCrmSync.php:24-28)
strengths: Finds all four root causes and fixes them with one coherent mechanism: an atomic conditional claim UPDATE plus a stale-claim window. No overlapping unique-lock layer
The 'Queued N' count stays accurate (probe confirmed 'Queued 0' on a re-run)
The job's WithoutOverlapping uses dontRelease()->expireAfter(120), which fixes both the stuck lock and the hot-loop release
Removes the try/catch. failed() records the error, and the idempotency guard prevents re-syncing

The original test file is left untouched and the new tests are in a separate file. They cover stale-claim re-queueing, failed_jobs through a real worker, and the normalize command across chunk boundaries with an already-normalized row

v.rationale: The root causes are: (1) handle() swallowed exceptions, so jobs never failed or retried; (2) the every-minute dispatch re-queued unsynced rows even while they were already queued; (3) the default withoutOverlapping() mutex lasts 24h; (4) chunk() pages over the column it is changing. All three implementations fix #3 with withoutOverlapping(N) and #4 with chunkById, and all remove the swallowed exception. They differ on #2 and on what happens after a failure. impl-1 combines an atomic DB claim with a 15-minute stale window, ShouldBeUnique and DeleteWhenMissingModels, using modern attributes. In probes it behaved best: one job per subscriber, re-queue after 15 minutes, and a deleted model no longer produces a failed_jobs row. Its flaw is a misleading count when the unique lock drops a claimed dispatch. impl-3 uses only the atomic claim, which is simpler and keeps the count accurate, and it has the best WithoutOverlapping configuration. It used older property-style config, has a weaker config-only test, and waits a slower 60 minutes before recovering. impl-2 relies only on ShouldBeUnique and leaves the dispatch command unchanged. That gives an inaccurate count, re-queues immediately after every failure (flooding failed_jobs and the CRM during long outages), and lets duplicates back in once a backlog outlives UniqueFor. Its end-to-end worker test is nonetheless the strongest single test.
